newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to lift price freeze Sept 16 - government.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to lift price freeze Sept 16 - government.

text.p: Ukraine will lift a price freeze imposed with the introduction of the new hryvnia currency after only two weeks, instead of waiting the full month as originally planned, the government said on Tuesday.

"The head of government (Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko) said the price freeze, brought in as part of the currency reform and originally intended to last until October 1, would be removed on September 16," a statement said.
The price freeze was intended to stop traders from taking advantage of the introduction of the new currency to raise prices of consumer goods.

The hryvnia was introduced on September 2, replacing the temporary karbovanets currency which will be withdrawn by September 16. The statement said this deadline would not be extended as the swap was going smoothly.
Western diplomats said the International Monetary Fund was unhappy with the measure because of its anti-free market nature.
"International financial organisations have been informed of the new decision," the release said.
Economists said the price freeze was hard to enforce because much of Ukraine's retail trade takes place on the black market.
Many stores, fearing the hryvnia would quickly devalue, had also rushed to raise prices in the week leading up to its debut.

But the hryvnia has actually been steady since it was introduced, and was unchanged again at 1.760 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Tuesday. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
